<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-security`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **2** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/position-renamed-holder-carry.ts`, `packages/spec/liveness/position.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

⛔ **3** release-owned page(s) name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v13.mdx`  _(via PositionSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/releases/v14.mdx`  _(via PositionSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via PositionSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/position-renamed-holder-carry.ts`, `packages/spec/liveness/position.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **175** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0e9ff949cb4bd2bb51716c4154e36699bd6d3a55` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `defa6009af6fd479659409d7b569332277305f83` — the merge of head `2f305516532bb157dedde77ff6afc43f6a403185` into base `0e9ff949cb4bd2bb51716c4154e36699bd6d3a55`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin defa6009af6fd479659409d7b569332277305f83 && git checkout defa6009af6fd479659409d7b569332277305f83
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 0e9ff949cb4bd2bb51716c4154e36699bd6d3a55 2f305516532bb157dedde77ff6afc43f6a403185 && git checkout -B drift-repro 0e9ff949cb4bd2bb51716c4154e36699bd6d3a55 && git merge --no-ff 2f305516532bb157dedde77ff6afc43f6a403185

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0e9ff949cb4bd2bb51716c4154e36699bd6d3a55
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 0e9ff949cb4bd2bb51716c4154e36699bd6d3a55` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `2f305516532bb157dedde77ff6afc43f6a403185`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/identity/position.zod.ts + packages/spec/liveness/position.json, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/position-renamed-holder-carry.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-start-hooks.ts

PR #33478 (`Refs #33301`, PR 1 of 2), read as the net diff against `origin/main` `0e9ff949` (merge base `19cc8976`; no commit between them touches a file this diff changes or cites). Card #33301 body and comments 6880960865, 6884480897, 6884987055 read. Text only: 6 files, +64/-35.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept set: unchanged — right.** `renamedFrom` is still `z.array(SnakeCaseIdentifierSchema).optional()`; the diff touches only its jsdoc and the string passed to `.describe()`. No value is newly accepted or refused.
- **Public surface: one description string — right.** The describe ships in `dist`, `json-schema/` and `src/**/*.zod.ts`, and `liveness/` is in `@objectstack/spec` `files[]`. No export, type or key changes.
- **Generated reference matches — right.** The `renamedFrom` cell of `content/docs/references/identity/position.mdx` at the head is character-for-character the concatenated describe string at the head (1203 characters each, compared by script over `git show` output; nothing built).
- **Liveness pointers unchanged — right.** In `liveness/position.json` the three `path#symbol` pointers (`position-renamed-holder-carry.ts#carryRenamedPositionHolders`, `position-renamed-from.ts#refuseSelfRenamedFrom`, `#refuseDishonestPositionRenamedFrom`), `status`, `verifiedAt`, `evidenceScope` and `note` are byte-identical; only the prose inside the first parenthesis changed.
- **plugin-security: comments only — right.** Both hunks sit inside a module jsdoc and `//` comments; no statement changes.
- **Check-runs on the head, as read on 2026-11-14:** 45 runs; 14 success (among them `Check Changeset`, `Spec property liveness`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `PR-body guards`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Check Documentation Links`), 9 skipped (opt-in or matrix placeholders), 22 still in progress (builds, type checks, the remaining lint families, `Test Core` 1/8 to 8/8, `Live E2E UI`), none failed. The in-progress runs have no conclusion yet, so they are no gate verdict yet; this record judges ① to ④ and does not stand in for them.

### ② Semver level

Clause-②: no — right. No accept set narrows or widens and no behaviour changes.

`@objectstack/spec` **patch** is the right level: a description string in a published schema changes and nothing else does.

No `@objectstack/plugin-security` changeset is right. Its `files[]` is `dist`, `README.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`. Its build is the root `tsup.config.ts` (esm + cjs, `sourcemap: true` with `dropSourcesContent`, dts): esbuild drops non-legal comments from the js, the maps carry no source text, and neither changed comment is attached to an exported declaration (one is the detached file-top module doc, the other sits inside `registerStartHooks`), so the d.ts does not carry them. Read from the manifest and build config, not built here; it agrees with the dev's measured grep over `dist`.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: empty.
- Deviation 1 (no plugin-security changeset against the order's line): answered in ②, the dev is right.
- Deviation 2 (the artifact reload has two payload shapes): confirmed in `packages/metadata/src/plugin.ts` on main. The file watcher calls `_reloadAndAnnounce(ctx, src, [src.path])`; the HMR POST handler (`setOnPostReload`, mounted only under a literal `NODE_ENV=development`) calls it with `body?.changed ?? [src.path]`. So "an artifact reload that names only its file" is the true form, and the card's flat "an artifact reload" was too wide. This is nit 1 of record 6880449445.
- Deviation 3 (the regenerated reference is in the diff): inside the claim's file surface ("a regenerated reference only if the describe renders there"); it does.
- Out-of-scope note (`renamedFrom.note` still says "named in the boot log"): still true of the boot run, outside the order's line; left as is, no escalation.
- The ADR-0150 D7 addendum sentence is not in this diff (Tier H, PR 2). Nothing in this diff touches a governed path.

### ④ Design judgment

Every changed sentence was read against the code on main: `positionRenameReloadScope`, `carryRenamedPositionHolders` and `createPositionRenameCarryRuns` in `position-renamed-holder-carry.ts`; the `kernel:bootstrapped` and `metadata:reloaded` hooks in `security-plugin-start-hooks.ts`; and the four announcers of `metadata:reloaded` (`marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts` install and uninstall, `objectql/src/plugin.ts` `announcePerItemPublish`, `runtime/src/domains/packages.ts` publish-drafts, `metadata/src/plugin.ts` `_reloadAndAnnounce`). No must-fix and no should-fix.

**`packages/spec/src/identity/position.zod.ts` (hits) — holds.**
- "at `kernel:bootstrapped` over every claim": `atBoot` runs with no `only`. True.
- "again on each `metadata:reloaded` after that over the claims of what the announcement names as registered: `app/ID` while the registry holds package `ID`, and `position/NAME`, whichever door announces them": `afterReload` returns before reading anything until `atBoot` has been called, reads `payload.changed`, admits `app/NAME` only when `registry.getPackage(NAME)` is non-null and `position/NAME` when `NAME` passes the grammar, with no test of who announced. True.
- Carried at once: install-local announces `app/manifestId` after registering; the per-item publish announces `type/name`; publish-drafts announces one `type/name` per published item. True.
- Carried at the next restart: an upgrade over a version still served leaves the old name in the catalog, so the claim is refused `still-declared`; `packages.ts` has one announce site, in publish-drafts, so install and enable are silent; the watcher names only the path. True.
- The describe says the same in plain words, carries no tracker number, and "A second run moves nothing" holds (once moved, no row names the old name).

**`packages/spec/liveness/position.json` — holds.** The evidence names both runs and the two admitted spellings; the refusal list is the code's six reasons.

**`position-renamed-holder-carry.ts`, "When it runs" — holds, and closes both nits of record 6880449445.** "whichever announcer sends it", "`NAME` is in the position-name grammar: the claims whose new name is `NAME`" (`only.positions.has(c.to)`), publish-drafts' unhidden `app/NAME` counting only for a held package id, and the two artifact-reload payload shapes all match the code.

**`security-plugin-start-hooks.ts` — holds.** The hook comment repeats the same four facts; the handler comment now names the per-item publish and publish-drafts beside the hot install, which is what the hook receives.

Tried against the texts and found sound: an absolute artifact path has its first slash at index 0 and is skipped; a relative path is another item type, or an `app/` name that is no held package, or a `position/` name that fails the grammar on its dot; a per-item publish of an `app` item whose name is a held package id is in scope, which "whichever announcer sends it" already says; an old name with one claim in scope and one outside is judged with both and refused `claimed-twice`.

**Nits (no effect on correctness or the contract):**

1. `position.zod.ts` jsdoc, "the runtime `POST /packages` install and enable routes": the enable route is `PATCH /packages/:id/enable`; only the install route (and its enable-on-install flag) is `POST /packages`. Neither announces, so the claim itself is true; the verb is loose. The wording is the card's.
2. `position.zod.ts` jsdoc, "is named in the run's log": a reload run that moves no holder row skips the left-behind read (`leftBehindOnlyWhenMoved`), so those references are named by a run that moves rows, or by the next boot run. The describe's "listed in the log" is not affected.
3. `position-renamed-holder-carry.ts`, "(a name no position serves has none)", and `liveness/position.json`, "reads ... only the `renamedFrom` of what the announcement names": claims are also built from a disabled package's positions, which the catalog does not serve (judged, refused `claimant-disabled`, nothing carried); and a reload run reads every position's `renamedFrom` and then judges only the scope's claims. Same outcome either way; only the wording is looser than the code.

All three are jsdoc or evidence prose inside reviewed files, so a fix moves the head: accepted deviations, or folded into PR 2's follow-up text. Nits alone end the round.

Reviewed-by: `session_01FEkQ5mswnWm181XgYcCUag`

**VERDICT: PASS**
